note: Machine-readable form of the palette(s) the pipeline knows how to resolve by key. docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md is the source of truth for what's canon; this file exists so a named palette can be ENFORCED on request. If they disagree, the markdown wins and this file is the bug. AMENDMENT 2026-07-28 (see that document's top banner): the strict global demichrome-4 lock recorded below is SUPERSEDED -- the game ships full colour by default (Emberkeep.Quantize=0) and demichrome-4 is now an explicit OPT-IN palette, not a default the pipeline forces. Nothing here invents what full colour's own rules are; there isn't a written standard yet (see aesthetic-direction.md AMENDMENT, 'consequences to expect, not yet resolved'). This file only stops assuming demichrome-4 by default -- it does not replace it with anything.

luma_model.why: Rec.709 luma on gamma-space sRGB values. The ramp is near-neutral, so quantizing by luma distance is more predictable than RGB distance and keeps the four values evenly separated. Linear-light luminance would crush the ramp toward the dark end and misassign midtones.

demichrome-4.name: 2-bit Demichrome

superseded.what_changed: No longer the enforced game-wide default. Full colour ships (Emberkeep.Quantize=0). This palette is kept in full, unchanged, and remains available as an explicit opt-in: name it in a request's canon.palette, pass it to pixelpipe.py's --palette, or pass --enforce-palette to Scripts/art/coverage.py. It is history the repo keeps, not a dead definition -- see docs/GDD-TODO.md and the pattern already used for Direction B in aesthetic-direction.md.

demichrome-4.authority: docs/art/aesthetic-direction.md (RESET banner, lines 8-46; see AMENDMENT 2026-07-28 at the top of that document for current status)
demichrome-4.scope: FORMER scope while locked (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-28): every sprite in the game — heroes, retinue, Still Legion, the Quiet, the Unwitnessed, UI, portraits, vignettes, no exceptions. CURRENT scope: opt-in only -- whatever explicitly names 'demichrome-4' (a request's canon.palette, a coverage/pixelpipe --palette flag). No sprite that opts into this ramp may introduce a fifth value or a palette-swapped variant without an explicit owner exception; that constraint is about this ramp specifically, not a claim about the whole game's colour policy anymore.

values.name: Demichrome Dark
values.role: darkest — outline, void, recess, ground state

values.name: Demichrome Steel
values.role: dark-mid — the game's only cold/armor/shadow value

values.name: Demichrome Bone
values.role: pale-mid — the game's only warm/skin/highlight value

values.name: Demichrome Pale
values.role: brightest — the game's only bright: lamps, eyes, marks, UI

mask.note: Transparency is not a value. Alpha must be binary (0 or 255) — the material is Unlit + Masked and partial alpha is the most common silent breakage.

ascii_legend.note: The characters art specs use to draw pixel maps in markdown (the silhouette guides in docs/art/*.md). 'pixelpipe.py authored' renders such a block straight to a PNG -- so a spec's silhouette guide is not a sketch of the sprite, it IS the sprite: on-palette by construction, correctly proportioned, and costing zero generations. Keep these characters stable; changing one invalidates every existing spec.

light_shift.rule: Light is a one-value-brighter shift along this same ladder, never a new hex. dark->steel, steel->bone, bone->pale, pale->pale.

dim_shift.rule: The inverse: one value darker along the same ladder, never a new hex. Added 2026-07-25 because the flame premise needs dimming at least as often as brightening -- units outside the leash render one value down (docs/narrative/FLAME-FOUNDATION.md 3a), and a guttering flame dims the bearer itself. Both are a 4-entry value remap driven by one scalar on the Unlit+Masked material, not a second texture.

dither.rule: 2x2 blocks minimum on anything that moves; 1px halftone is reserved for static UI and portraits. 1px dither on a moving sprite shimmers at horde scale.

trial_palettes.note: Candidate ramps for the Emberkeep.Palette dial (task-043) — NOT canon. demichrome-4 above is the historical / opt-in ramp (see its 'superseded' field), not the enforced direction anymore as of the 2026-07-28 colour reversal; these trial entries exist so a candidate can still be judged in PIE at horde density instead of on a swatch, same as before. The index here is the CVar value and must match the GSwarmPalettePresets table in Rendering/SwarmRenderActor.cpp. TO ADD ONE: append an entry here and one row there — every entry is still just 4 hexes, even though task-057 generalized the live dial to 2-8 steps (see palette_steps_generalization below); ResamplePaletteColor stretches these 4 control points to whatever step count is live, so a candidate's cost never changes.

palette_steps_generalization.owner_call: 2026-07-28 — 'explore options without the color gate'; when asked what that meant, chose BYPASS QUANTIZATION ENTIRELY over just more values.
palette_steps_generalization.Emberkeep.Quantize: [0..1], default 1. 0 shows the raw lit scene (flame lift + world-anchored dither survive, only the posterise value-collapse goes). Locked default is byte-identical to pre-task-057 output.
palette_steps_generalization.Emberkeep.PaletteSteps: [2..8], default 4. How many values the posterise collapses onto. At 4 (the locked default), Threshold1/2/3 and Palette0..3 above are pushed completely unchanged — this file's 4-hex entries are not reinterpreted at all. Away from 4, SwarmRenderActor.cpp derives fresh evenly-spaced thresholds and resamples each entry's 4 hexes across the new count, so no palette here needs an 8-hex variant to support the full step range.

trial_palettes.how_to_judge: min_luma_gap is the number that matters. It is the tightest step on the ramp, and it is what carries friend/foe readability at 700 units — demichrome's 0.218 is the bar. A palette that photographs better and reads worse in a wave has lost.

entries.name: 2-bit Demichrome (historical / opt-in — no longer the enforced default, see palettes.demichrome-4.superseded)
Eulbink (4-value cut)
entries.note: Cut from the 7-colour set, whose bottom three blues sit within 0.10 luma and cannot all survive as distinct values. Separates BETTER than the incumbent. Would also close open decision L11 (docs/RENDERING-LIGHTING.md:705) — the flame pool currently reads warm because it grades through Bone; a blue->white ramp gives a white pool without a palette exception. Tonally cold, for a game about carrying fire.

entries.name: Rust Gold (4-value cut)
entries.note: Cut from the 8-colour set, which CANNOT work whole under a luminance quantizer: #202020/#331c17 are luma 0.125/0.128 and #563226/#393939 are 0.223/0.224, so those pairs collapse into one bucket. The full set separates by HUE, which needs the Phase B index pipeline (task-041). This 4-cut is a proper value ramp and gives the warm tone without it.

retired_hexes.note: Hexes voided by the 2026-07-12 reset. The validator rejects any request or linked spec that cites one. Several are still present in stale docs (CLASSES.md:78 cites #f0b84a) — that is why this list exists.

shape_carriers.note: The four shape-only bright carriers survive the reset (docs/art/hero-palettes.md §3). With hue gone game-wide, these are load-bearing: they are how the single bright value stays legible as four different things.
